title: The Hare and the Hedgehog
text:
On a fine Sunday morning, a hedgehog went out to look at his turnip field and met a hare. The hare, who thought very well of himself, mocked the hedgehog's short crooked legs. Stung, the hedgehog challenged him to a race and bet him a gold coin and a bottle of brandy that he would win. The hare laughed and agreed.

The hedgehog went home first, he said, for breakfast. There he told his wife to come with him to the field. Hedgehogs look so alike that no one could tell husband and wife apart. He placed her at the far end of a furrow and went back to the near end, where the hare was waiting.

The hare ran down his furrow like the wind. The hedgehog went a few steps and then sat still. When the hare reached the far end, the hedgehog's wife rose up from the other furrow and called out that she was already there.

The hare could not believe it. He demanded another run and raced back. At the other end, the hedgehog popped up: already here. The hare ran again and again, seventy three times, and each time a hedgehog was waiting. On the seventy fourth run he collapsed and died. The hedgehog took the gold coin and the brandy home, and lived happily with his wife.
lesson: Do not accept a contest on your opponent's terms when you can set the terms yourself. And never assume that the one who looks slow has no plan.
people: A hedgehog, his wife, a hare
source: Brothers Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 187, from a Low German tale published by Wilhelm Schroder
